key_insight: QiT transfers quantum-inspired ideas into a standard Transformer by using angle-based features, cosine-style attention, and multiplicative gating to model periodic similarities without running a quantum circuit.
engineering_relevance: The method offers a scalable classical baseline for vision systems that want quantum-motivated inductive biases while keeping normal Transformer training and inference costs.
method: Angle-inspired token encoding maps image patches into trigonometric features analogous to rotation-based quantum states.
Self-attention operates on these periodic features to approximate a cosine kernel similar to quantum fidelity measures.
Gated multiplicative modules emulate interaction terms from variational quantum circuits using differentiable tensor ops.
evidence_signal: Across image-classification benchmarks, QiT is competitive with a matched classical Transformer and QiT-B reports 78.3% top-1 ImageNet-1K accuracy with 45.7M parameters and 11.5 GFLOPs.
watch_item: QiT is not a quantum accelerator and does not provide quantum speedup, so gains depend on whether the added inductive bias outweighs standard Transformer complexity and tuning costs.
paper_title: QiT: Quantum-Inspired Transformer for Visual Recognition Task
